structural_tests.rationale: Combine legacy operating contraction and higher maintenance with acquired fixed costs, customer attrition, opening debt and extraordinary claims. Fund $250m closure when acquired owner cash remains negative. No invented operating savings or loan-principal recovery supports survival.

Execute the same joint operating and acquired-claim shock with no parent credit access. Keep the operating buffer unchanged, preserve creditor payments, fund acquired closure and receive neither artificial savings nor financing-receivable proceeds.

Require the full $950m opening acquired-debt and recourse payment with elective staging disabled. Acquisition-adjusted opening resources of $2,229,743,689 leave $1,279,743,689 against the unchanged $1.3bn operating-plus-minority buffer. Timely committed credit must supply $20,256,311 before the deadline, preventing the procurement restriction. Borrowed cash is counted once and incurs interest. Compare with the identical no-credit state, which pays the same senior claims and executes the explicit earnings-sacrificing operating response.

Test a materially deeper three-year domestic assignment contraction with weaker international activity, fee resistance, stranded administration and impaired new-capital productivity. Later stabilization preserves the smaller activity base; shorter continuation tests further competitive fade independently.

Permitting constraints, insurer workflows and buyer depth can sustain assignments and productive deployment beyond the normalization phase. Test stronger geographic activity and faster cohort maturation while continuing to charge replacement, cash taxes, working capital and growth investment.

Combine legacy erosion with high acquired fixed costs, expensive maintenance and poor new returns. The acquired trial fails and incurs maximum modeled closure cash; legacy operations and surviving creditor claims continue independently. Retained financial resources remain separately realizable.

Execute severe financing withdrawal with $40m forgone revenue, weak interest avoidance, lost connected customers and high lost contribution, jointly with legacy contraction, unavailable credit and opening acquired claims. Fund a $250m operating exit if losses persist rather than capitalize negative owner support. Compensation remains a real cost and a further $100m intervening drain reduces resources.

Replace acquired external borrowing with parent cash and maintain the estimated opening net financing book throughout the projection. Carve baseline financing earnings out of aggregate ACV earnings, then restore forecast fees less cash servicing and credit losses. Cleared collections fund replacement originations; additional parent capital replaces written-off principal. No book growth, warehouse renewal or principal realization is assumed. Nonlending investment alone receives target incremental operating returns. Preserve matched maturation and parent payout settings for comparison with withdrawal.

Return initial surplus after preserving operating cash, minority reserves, the permanent legacy-claim reserve and the full deferred closure estimate. Thereafter distribute positive annual cash after all modeled funding uses, with remaining surplus distributed once in year 13. Reduced financial balances earn less interest. Creditor and closure obligations are identical to the retained-cash policy.

Keep the $1.2bn upper operating requirement plus minority reserve with unavailable parent credit, legacy contraction and severe acquired payments. No buffer reduction or access-triggered operating savings is permitted; acquired exit pays its full stressed cash cost.

Retain half of annual distributable surplus after the integration holdback while funding larger organic investment at weaker incremental returns and a lower cash yield. This tests continuing deployment and delayed capital return without inventing a complete prohibition on payouts until 2039. Only remaining unreserved cash is released at the final audited projection boundary. Creditor, operating and minority reserves remain unavailable for distribution; the same cash is never both invested and paid out.

Combine unavailable parent credit, recurring mature activity erosion, general operating and replacement inflation, weak incremental returns and large surviving-claim demands. Nominal pricing responds to the general inflation regime but activity contracts and fixed expense pressure remains; maintenance receives no automatic cash offset. Retain the permanent claim reserve and deferred closure schedule without assuming recovery or legal discharge.

Raise replacement-capital inflation independently while holding each case's realized yield and operating input inflation unchanged. This directly tests whether higher sustaining cash needs reduce payouts and continuation earnings rather than cancelling through an automatic cash-generation addback.

Copart's permitting and yard-utilization lags and ACV's unproven customer payback support testing slower maturation alongside weaker incremental returns. Retain the stressed revenue productivity, first-producing-year fraction, maintenance and returns. Reduce subsequent earnings growth to 3%, fading to 2% and then 1%: delayed deployment and weaker productivity constrain later expansion too. In the high case, the surviving ACV deployment mix produces a 5.55% incremental parent-equity return, so every continuation growth phase remains fundable. Keep all explicit investment charges, creditor payments and liquidity reserves. FY2026's nearly flat revenue and lower operating income counter automatic catch-up; review against new-yard utilization and postclosing ACV cash after compensation and sustaining investment.

Correlate domestic assignment loss, weaker international activity, fee resistance and stranded costs with unavailable parent credit and larger acquired-claim payments. Defer optional new growth, preserve creditor payments and buffers, and execute the already modeled ACV closure response when its cash test fails.

Test persistent domestic activity loss throughout years 6–13 together with initial weakness, fee resistance, stranded operating costs, replacement inflation, unavailable parent credit and acquired senior claims. The late domestic factor of 0.97 precedes the additional fee response; eight such years imply approximately 22% cumulative activity loss before that response. Domestic nominal yield rises 3%, while operating cash costs rise 3% and replacement capital rises 4%; pricing therefore does not automatically preserve owner earnings. Defer optional investment, execute the existing target continuation/closure decision and retain all contractual-tail payments. Existing liquid resources fund the senior waterfall; no refinancing, owner contribution or receivable recovery is assumed. Keep the equity hurdle unchanged so operating and funding shocks enter cash flows once.

Test an investment phase rather than closing solely because current cash is negative. Assume $90m of annual operating expense improvement, recognize 35% in year 2 and the remainder in year 3, and evaluate continuation on prospective mature cash after ordinary compensation and maintenance. Parent payouts, financing withdrawal, debt payment, recourse funding, claim reserves, growth budgets and cash access retain their main settings. Interim losses consume parent cash; they receive no separate addback or automatic financing.

Matched counterhypothesis to acv_maturation_with_matched_parent_policy: set unverified operating improvement to zero and keep the same parent payout policy. The existing mature-cash decision then selects continuation or closure from operating economics, while modeled closure, servicing and surviving claims remain funded. Compare operating cash, retained resources and distributions, not merely aggregate value.

Combine persistent compensation inflation with slower production and weaker new-capital returns. Talent retention and delayed yard/software utilization can occur together; nominally fixed SBC would conceal their joint burden. Preserve the same parent payout policy and funding reserves, charge compensation once, and do not offset replacement-cost pressure with unsupported pricing.

Raise prospective cash taxes to 30% while holding normalization_tax_rate, revenue, pretax operating-cost drivers, maintenance and growth outlays unchanged. Reduced FDII benefits and higher jurisdictional burdens can reduce shareholder cash without improving operating efficiency. Recompilation must show unchanged initial pretax cost pools and cohort calibration, higher taxes wherever taxable earnings are positive, and nonincreasing aggregate equity value relative to the unchanged contract.

Test continued favorable tax treatment at 18% against the matched 30% tax alternative. Keep pretax capacity, operating costs, investment and financing policy identical. Initial calibrated cost pools and pretax cohort earnings must match exactly between these alternatives; only prospective taxes and their subsequent cash-balance consequences may differ. This distinguishes tax benefits from operating productivity.

Execute unavailable warehouse refinancing and parent facilities together with loss of the entire opening finance book, collection deferral and weaker auction economics. External acquired debt is prepaid before these later lending decisions. Collections constrain replacement deployment; actual losses require explicit cash replacement, lower parent distributions and a renewed continuation decision. If mature acquired cash fails, the existing closure branch stops originations and charges closure and surviving claims. Borrower principal loss is distinct from uncapped contractual indemnities, which retain their separate stress charges.

Compare withdrawal with the fixed-book continuing-finance alternative using identical parent payouts, acquired debt repayment, extraordinary claim funding and nonlending maturation. Remove the baseline financing earnings slice, cease new lending, and retain the previously modeled customer, assurance and surviving-claim consequences. No financing principal recovery is credited. The comparison measures forgone explicit fee earnings, avoided servicing and credit losses, customer damage and capital replacement needs without changing payout timing.

Preserve this test's identity but eliminate its former debt-staging mechanism. Change only facility access relative to the matched timely-credit squeeze, with elective staging fixed at zero. Pay the same $950m senior claims at opening. Restrict half of parent principal procurement: the $51.382m reported inventory anchor yields $25.691m less replenishment-related buffer requirement, while $2m implementation cash leaves a $3.435m opening cushion. Sacrifice $350m annual trading revenue and $32m after-tax contribution; retain shared overhead and maintenance. Restore normal procurement and the full reserve in year two using operating receipts before payouts. No inventory proceeds, lender waiver or later receipt funds the opening payment.

Test whether parent-funded lending remains economically attractive when fee realization weakens and servicing becomes more expensive. Hold the opening net loan book, baseline carve-out, nonlending maturation and parent payout policy fixed. Annual fees of $12m, servicing of $12m and credit losses of 20% jointly test unit economics; the operating continuation decision must then execute continued support or closure, including the full contractual tail.

Test the opposing explanation that recurring financed-customer fees justify maintaining the fixed net loan book. Hold baseline financing allocations, debt repayment, nonlending maturation, credit-loss rates and parent payouts unchanged while increasing forecast annual financing fees to $40m. Revenue, earnings and cash must respond from the first consolidated year. No generic incremental operating return or loan-book expansion supplies the improvement.

Test the no-credit intermediate squeeze with a larger operating restriction, higher implementation expenditure and greater lost contribution. Require the same full opening senior payment and unchanged ex ante buffer. Curtailing three quarters of procurement reduces the inventory-related requirement by $38.5365m, costs $5m immediately, and sacrifices $600m revenue and $75m after-tax annual contribution under the adverse program estimates. This tests whether the operating response remains funded while materially damaging earnings; no debt deferral or inventory-sale cash is available.

flags.detail: Over 75% of this component present value comes from exit realization.

hypotheses.explanation: Permitting, owned yard coverage, insurer workflows and buyer depth can preserve the parent franchise while nominal pricing funds expenses and investment cohorts add cash. Persistence is tested through activity, pricing and independently forecast expenses rather than a flat earnings multiplier.
hypotheses.counterevidence: FY2026 operating income declined despite nearly flat revenue; domestic service revenue weakness and customer bargaining contradict automatic persistence.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: FY2027-FY2029 comparable activity, realization and cash expense reconciliation supports mature revenue growth exceeding expense growth while lagged funded cohorts earn after-maintenance cash returns within the declared range.

hypotheses.explanation: Domestic assignments can continue declining after catastrophe comparisons normalize because insurers gain bargaining power, direct purchasing bypasses auctions or rival capacity attracts supply. Higher realizations can conceal activity losses while fixed staffing, administration and replacement spending reduce owner cash. The main forecast now permits continued late erosion; the joint persistent-loss alternative tests a substantially worse path without assuming a lower capitalization multiple.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Permitting constraints, owned yards, international buyers and integrated title workflows may preserve assignments and allow costs to adjust. FY2026 comparisons also include catastrophe and mix effects.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Track successive annual domestic service revenue together with disclosed revenue per car and assignment information. Continued assignment losses after identified catastrophe comparisons lapse support persistent competitive erosion. Compare consolidated annual revenue and OCF with the frozen FY2029 and FY2032 forecasts to identify whether revenue delivery converts into cash; do not infer volume recovery from stable nominal revenue alone.

hypotheses.explanation: ACV's losses may partly reflect building technology and territory density whose later revenue can support lower operating costs. The main forecast gives that claim no savings. A matched alternative stages a bounded $90m annual expense improvement across years 2 and 3, tests prospective cash after ordinary compensation and maintenance, and retains parent-funded support before maturation. Closure is evaluated with identical financing, claim reserves and parent payout fractions.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Latest-half marketplace units grew slowly, SBC remains substantial, and financing withdrawal may damage auction participation. Management's investment narrative does not establish successful payback or permit eliminating required maintenance.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Comparable postclosing ACV expense and cash reconciliations show the assumed improvement while repeat transactions, assurance outcomes and customer retention remain adequate. Failure to improve after two complete cycles favors closure and refutes the modeled investment-phase explanation.

hypotheses.explanation: Collateral failures, assurance claims and surviving contractual duties can consume acquired resources and require parent-funded losses during a legacy operating contraction.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Large parent liquid resources and cessation of new target lending can contain the modeled funding need; historical receivables may collect well.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Closing debt, restricted cash, repurchase notices and realized runoff establish whether net cash demands remain within the declared estimates.

hypotheses.explanation: Removing dealer credit can reduce bidding and seller engagement, lowering auction, transport, data and assurance revenue. Assurance is a distinct retained product with its own claims cost; withdrawing lending does not eliminate assurance by definition.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Customers may substitute outside financing and retain inspection, auction and assurance services with little attrition.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Compare financed and unfinanced customer cohorts after withdrawal using active bidders, repeat sellers, auction units, assurance attachment and contribution after claims. Identify lending fees separately from assurance revenue.

hypotheses.explanation: Persistent retention may be the actual policy while acquisition outcomes and claims become observable. Retained surplus earns cash returns unless explicitly deployed, and its principal remains part of the ownership realization.
hypotheses.counterevidence: The recent large repurchase demonstrates an alternative use, while additional acquisitions could consume cash at uncertain returns.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: FY2027-FY2028 cash, Treasury holdings, repurchases and acquisition spending distinguish persistent retention, distribution and new deployment.

hypotheses.explanation: A funded acquired-business exit can stop new commercial losses while existing obligations survive. This differs from either automatic operating cost savings after loss of credit or disappearance of the legacy business after an equity failure.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Employee rights, lease commitments and ongoing servicing could delay cessation or require more cash than estimated.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: A complete exit reconciliation establishes cessation of new exposure, remaining service duration and cash costs; costs above $250m or material support after year two refute the modeled response.

hypotheses.explanation: Stopping new ACV operations can end new operating losses while leaving leases, servicing transition, indemnity and reinstatement costs payable for substantially longer. Parent equity value therefore depends on both operating results and the later cash burden, rather than an assumed year-two discharge.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Verified transfers, releases or favorable runoff could shorten the tail and reduce cash needs; significant breaches could instead exceed the modeled amounts.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: A reconciled postclosing schedule of contractual payments, servicing migration and asserted surviving claims, compared with cash payments and restricted resources.

hypotheses.explanation: Permitting, opening and software adoption can defer production, while recurring talent costs continue rising. Productive capital must generate sufficient later revenue and after-tax cash to cover both replacement capital and compensation. The revised cohort graph and terminal bridge make these consequences explicit.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Existing-network additions can mature faster and automation can restrain compensation. Conversely, acquisitions and greenfield yards may need more time and capital than these bounds allow.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Opening cohorts' revenue and cash after maintenance over their first two producing fiscal years, together with annual compensation and share reconciliations, distinguish productive delayed deployment from continuing support of weak economics.

hypotheses.explanation: Replacing warehouse and revolver funding can preserve financed-customer engagement, but parent equity must support the loan book and replace credit losses. Underwrite a fixed net book rather than assigning generic operating growth returns to lending capital. Remove the financing earnings embedded in aggregate ACV forecasts, then rebuild fees, servicing and credit losses explicitly. Continuing lending wins only if those net earnings and preserved customer contribution justify its funding burden.
hypotheses.counterevidence: The filing reports historical finance-receivable growth and concentrated losses, but does not establish a standalone financing margin. A fixed-book policy may sacrifice attractive demand or prove operationally difficult. Lower losses and higher fee realization could favor continued lending; servicing and collateral problems could favor withdrawal.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Reconcile acquired financing fees, average net receivables, cleared principal collections, originations, write-offs and consolidated servicing costs over two annual cycles. A fixed net book must show collections plus explicit equity loss replacement funding its originations. Compare fee earnings after servicing and losses with customer contribution lost under withdrawal.

hypotheses.explanation: A temporary restriction on principal vehicle purchasing can reduce inventory replenishment risk before an operating-buffer deadline while preserving the predominantly consignment auction network. Its economic cost is foregone trading revenue and contribution plus implementation cash. Subsequent operating receipts restore the original buffer before procurement resumes.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Existing commitments or shared customer relationships may prevent a timely restriction or make the damage exceed the direct trading contribution. The inventory anchor establishes scale, not a contractual right or guaranteed liquidity reduction.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: The next filing's inventory, vehicle-sales spread, purchase commitments and operating cash show whether procurement exposure declined before the deadline and whether the original buffer was rebuilt without creditor deferral or inventory-sale proceeds.

forecast_commitments.scope: Copart consolidated annual operating cash flow for August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027, including ACV only after October 16, 2026. Compare cash_y1 to annual OCF, identifying forecast-versus-actual financing policy, assurance claims, working capital, cash taxes and restructuring cash. Maintenance, growth and cash-equivalent compensation funding remain separate shareholder cash uses; do not compare this annual flow to a quarter.

Copart consolidated annual revenue from August 1, 2027 through July 31, 2028. Include acquired commercial revenue only in scenarios passing the explicit continuation test. Compare actual retained or exited ACV activity separately; never grade this annual forecast against a quarter or GMV.

Copart consolidated annual operating cash from August 1, 2027 through July 31, 2028. Reconcile actual compensation funding, acquired closure cash and interest to the modeled cash-generation boundary. Acquisition consideration, debt principal, growth investment and owner payouts remain separate. An acquired operational exit must be tested against its cash cost and remaining obligations, not simply marked as zero support.

Copart consolidated reporting-date usable cash at July 31, 2027. Reconcile reported restricted cash and unmonetized Treasury holdings to modeled monetized usable resources; identify actual debt draws, acquisition payments, claim payments and retained operating cash. Do not compare this balance with an annual flow.

Copart consolidated annual OCF for August 1, 2028 through July 31, 2029. Reconcile reported OCF to the model's parent cash generation boundary, including modeled financing interest, normal operating balances, funded compensation and closure or legacy-claim cash. Maintenance and growth remain separately funded uses. Compare jointly with p3_revenue to test forecast cash expense responsiveness; do not infer operating success from float release.

Copart consolidated annual revenue for August 1, 2028 through July 31, 2029. Reconcile acquisition changes, ACV continuation or closure, currency, catastrophe mix, comparable activity and revenue per unit. Compare the annual observation with this independently forecast revenue, not with a quarter or auction GMV.

Copart, reported consolidated annual revenue, including subsidiaries consolidated during the fiscal year. Compare the complete annual flow with p6_revenue. Separately explain acquisitions, disposals and currency changes. This replaces the unsupported standalone facility cash-expense field and tests the first year of the disputed late activity phase.

Copart, reported consolidated annual net cash provided by operating activities. Compare the complete annual flow with p6_cash, jointly with p6_revenue; retain the disclosed reconciliation of taxes, compensation, operating balances and surviving-claim payments. Explain classification differences explicitly. This replaces the nonexistent incremental-capital observation field. Cash weakness despite revenue delivery challenges the modeled operating-cost and working-capital conversion mechanisms.
